where $\mathsf C$ is a constant skew-symmetric Coriolis matrix. Setting $n=1$, $u>0$, $G=0$, and $\mathsf C=0$ recovers $\mathcal E_1$. The rotating planar cubic model $\mathcal E_2$ takes $n=2$, $m=3$, $\kappa=K$, and $\mathsf C=f\mathcal J$, where $\mathcal J(u,v)=(-v,u)$.
